post.title: Space Walk: Agent Session Replay
post.hook: Your agent's session log, replayed as light moving across a night map of the repo.
post.summary: Space Walk is a Go and React tool that replays Claude Code, Codex, and pi sessions on a 3D map of the codebase, with an optional LLM judge. The repo also holds a small Next.js solar-system starter.
post.writeup:
## What it is
Space Walk is XO Labs' fork of mindwalk (MIT). One Go binary reads Claude Code, Codex, and pi session logs and draws the repository as a night map. Playback shows where the agent searched, read, and edited: those files glow, everything else stays dark. Viewing is fully local.

## Why
A session log records what an agent did, but not how it understood the task. Reading raw JSONL does not tell you which parts of the repo it treated as relevant, or whether its footprint matched the scope you had in mind.

## How it works
Three artifacts stay separate: a normalized trace, a deterministic citymap of the repo, and an evaluation report. Each agent format sits behind its own adapter. The UI offers Tree and Terrain views, a playback deck, timeline marks, subagent lenses, and a file inspector.

Evaluation is opt-in. A judge CLI (claude or codex) runs with no tools in up to two calls: one drafts a task rubric from your own requests, one scores four fixed dimensions (exploration, scope, wandering, verification) plus the rubric. Verdicts are derived mechanically from finding severities, never decided by the LLM. Rubrics are capped at 6 tasks and 3 to 12 criteria.

## Findings
The brand palette failed as a categorical encoding on the night surface: seen and edited sat at a normal-vision ΔE of 11.1, below the 15 floor. So the shipped colors are OKLCH derivations, validated for color-vision separation and contrast.

## Also in the folder
A small Next.js 16 and React Three Fiber starter called solar-system, still the default create-next-app scaffold.

## Open questions
No releases are published yet, so installation is from source only. The solar-system starter has no scene yet.
